newsitem.title: UK: Norway's Gullfaks down to 10 pct capacity - trade.
newsitem.headline: Norway's Gullfaks down to 10 pct capacity - trade.

text.p: Statoil's 570,000 barrel a day (bpd) North Sea Gullfaks oilfield system was running at just 10 percent of capacity on Friday after bad weather prevented offshore loadings and storage reached capacity, trade sources familiar with the company's operations said.
Output at Statoil's Gullfaks A, B and C platforms and Saga Petroleum's Tordis, which flows via Gullfaks C, was reduced to a combined 60,000 bpd amid high winds and swell, the trade source said.
A Statoil spokeswoman confirmed output was being reduced at Gullfaks B and C after an earlier reduction to 10 percent at Gullfaks A. But she was unable to give exact output levels for B and C.
Statoil earlier had reduced output at the 800,000 bpd Statfjord system, which includes production from Saga's 230,000 bpd Snorre.
But an improvement in weather conditions allowed Statfjord liftings to resume by early afternoon and production to restart at Snorre.
